My values for the schools are w=$53, x=$79, y=$73, z=$63. My priority ranks at each school are w:1, x:2, y:1, z:2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

I need to consider what happens if I'm rejected from my top choices. My highest value school is x ($79). However, it's likely *very* competitive. My rank at x is only 2, meaning many others are higher priority. Therefore, I'm likely to be rejected from x initially.

If rejected from x, my next choice is y ($73). I have a rank of 1 at y, which is excellent. Given the general applicant preference for y, it's still likely to be competitive, but my rank of 1 significantly increases my chances of acceptance. This is a crucial safety net.

If rejected from y as well (which is possible, given the popularity), my next choice is w ($53). My rank at w is 1, so I'd be accepted. While w isn't my highest value, it's better than being unmatched.

Finally, z ($63) is my last resort. I have a rank of 2 there.

Given this, I will rank x first, hoping to get in, but prioritizing y as my second choice due to my high rank there. This maximizes my chances of getting a good outcome. I'm banking on my rank of 1 at y being enough to secure a spot if x doesn't work out. w is my safety net.
